content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Upgrading MongoDB"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a comprehensive guide to upgrading your MongoDB deployment. Upgrading ensures you benefit from the latest features, performance improvements, and security patches. Before proceeding, always back up your data."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Planning the Upgrade"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Careful planning is crucial for a smooth upgrade. Consider these factors:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Review the MongoDB release notes for the target version. Pay close attention to any backward-incompatible changes or deprecated features."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check the compatibility of your applications and drivers with the new MongoDB version. Upgrade drivers if necessary."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Assess your current deployment architecture (standalone, replica set, sharded cluster) and choose the appropriate upgrade procedure."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Plan for downtime. Minimize impact by using rolling upgrades for replica sets and sharded clusters."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Backup Your Data"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before any upgrade, create a full backup of your MongoDB data. This allows you to restore your data in case of unforeseen issues."},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use `mongodump` to create a logical backup:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"mongodump --host <hostname> --port <port> --username <username> --password <password> --authenticationDatabase admin --out <backup_directory>"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, for larger datasets, consider using file system snapshots if your storage system supports them."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Upgrading a Standalone MongoDB Instance"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"For a standalone instance, the upgrade process involves stopping the existing instance, replacing the binaries, and restarting the instance."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stop the MongoDB instance: `mongod --shutdown`"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Download the new MongoDB binaries from the MongoDB website."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Replace the old binaries with the new ones. Ensure the new binaries are in your system's PATH."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Restart the MongoDB instance: `mongod --dbpath <data_directory>`"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Upgrading a Replica Set"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Upgrading a replica set involves a rolling upgrade, where you upgrade each member one at a time to minimize downtime."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Upgrade secondary members first. For each secondary:"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"rs.stepDown() # Step down the secondary (if it's the current secondary)"},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"mongod --shutdown # Shutdown the mongod process"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Replace the old binaries with the new ones."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Restart the mongod process with the new binaries."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Wait for the secondary to recover and become SECONDARY again."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Once all secondaries are upgraded, step down the primary:"},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"rs.stepDown() # Step down the primary"},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Upgrade the old primary (now a secondary) using the same procedure as the other secondaries."},{"order":31,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Upgrading a Sharded Cluster"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"Upgrading a sharded cluster requires a more complex rolling upgrade procedure. Upgrade the config servers first, then the shard servers, and finally the mongos routers."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Upgrade the config servers. If using a replica set for config servers, follow the replica set upgrade procedure."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Upgrade the shard servers. Follow the replica set upgrade procedure for each shard."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Upgrade the mongos routers. Stop each mongos instance, replace the binaries, and restart the instance."},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Post-Upgrade Tasks"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"After the upgrade, perform the following tasks:"},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Run `db.upgradeCheck()` in the `admin` database to check for any required post-upgrade operations."},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Update feature compatibility version (FCV) to the new version: `db.adminCommand( { setFeatureCompatibilityVersion: '<new_version>' } )`"},{"order":40,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor your deployment for any issues and ensure that your applications are functioning correctly."},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"Remember to consult the official MongoDB documentation for detailed instructions and specific considerations for your environment."}]
